\section[negociar]{negociar — to negotiate}

\label{lesson:ES-C634-negociar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the luxury, then the Spanish for free of charge.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: negociar}
\textbf{negociar} — \textquotedblleft{}to negotiate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Vamos a negociar el precio.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We are going to negotiate the price.}
\end{quote}

Regular -ar verb.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{negociar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{negotiari} 'to do business', built on \emph{negotium} 'business', from \emph{nec} 'not' and \emph{otium} 'leisure' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{negociar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{negociar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{negociar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the luxury, then the Spanish for free of charge, then say \emph{negociar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does negociar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To negotiate\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la negociación]{la negociación — the negotiation}

\label{lesson:ES-C634-negociacion}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for free of charge, then the Spanish for to negotiate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la negociación}
\textbf{la negociación} — \textquotedblleft{}the negotiation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La negociación duró tres días.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The negotiation lasted three days.}
\end{quote}

Often plural: \emph{las negociaciones}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{negociación} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{negotiatio} 'business, trade', built on \emph{negotium}, from \emph{otium} 'leisure' with \emph{nec} 'not' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for free of charge, then the Spanish for to negotiate, then say \emph{la negociación} again

\section[ceder]{ceder — to give way, to give in; to hand over}

\label{lesson:ES-C634-ceder}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to negotiate, then the Spanish for the negotiation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: ceder}
\textbf{ceder} — \textquotedblleft{}to give way, to give in; to hand over\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Al final, mi padre cedió.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{In the end, my father gave in.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Ceda el paso} on a road sign — give way.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ceder} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{cedere} 'to go away, to yield' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[acordar]{acordar — to agree on}

\label{lesson:ES-C634-acordar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the negotiation, then the Spanish for to give way.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: acordar}
\textbf{acordar} — \textquotedblleft{}to agree on\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Acordamos una fecha.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We agreed on a date.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Acordar algo} — to agree on it. Stem change o$\to$ue.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{acordar} is inherited from spoken Latin \emph{accordare}, built on \emph{cor} 'heart' (EtymDB): to agree is to be of one heart.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the negotiation, then the Spanish for to give way, then say \emph{acordar} again

\section[persuadir]{persuadir — to persuade}

\label{lesson:ES-C634-persuadir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to give way, then the Spanish for to agree on.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: persuadir}
\textbf{persuadir} — \textquotedblleft{}to persuade\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Me persuadió para firmar.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{She persuaded me to sign.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Persuadir a alguien para} or \emph{de} + infinitive.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{persuadir} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{persuadere} 'to convince', built from \emph{per} and \emph{suadere} 'to advise' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
